done_when: Close's review and plan reads do not wait for an agent place, and a test run limited to a few named test files does not wait for the test place

findings.body: Raise: Functional — `few_tests` checks only the command tokens for a doctest option, then grants a free run when at most five conventionally named test files are selected. In a client with `test = "pytest tests src"` and an unchanged `pyproject.toml` containing `addopts = "--doctest-modules"`, five changed test files qualify even though pytest also runs source doctests. `fasttest.py:31–54` shows that pytest options can come from configuration or `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`; `fasttest.py:276–279` counts only `test_*.py` and `*_test.py`. An explicitly named file outside those patterns, such as `tests/acceptance.py`, likewise remains in the command without being counted. These runs can exceed the five-file limit while another run holds the only test place. This is new evidence beyond the previously reported command-line doctest case.
findings.title: Configured pytest collection can bypass the test place

findings.body: Raise: Gate — The supplied proof list names only the doctest-option and five-file test-lane cases. It omits both remaining Done-when details: a close review and a plan read starting without an agent place. The changed command-level test at this line exercises those behaviours, but neither has an entry in the required whole-change proof list.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: small test runs skip the test queue only when the test command has no doctest option; reviews and plan reads still skip the agent queue

why: A 2-minute review waits about 10 minutes for an agent place and a worker's small test run queues for the single test place
